context: In a team #launch-prep channel, Sarah posts at 9:45 PM: 'Just finished the 4th client deck revision... I honestly don't know if my brain can handle another last-minute requirement pivot. I'm exhausted and feeling completely defeated by this sprint.'
prompt: How do you respond to Sarah to MATCH her current conversation state according to Duhigg's framework?

options.text: Don't worry Sarah! We're almost at the finish line! Tomorrow is going to be amazing and everyone loves your work! 🚀🎉
options.feedback: MISMATCH (Toxic Positivity): Forcing bright cheerfulness invalidates Sarah's real exhaustion and pushes her further into isolation.

options.text: I hear you Sarah. You've been carrying a massive load on these decks and it sounds incredibly overwhelming and draining. Thank you for pushing through.
options.feedback: CORRECT (Emotional Matching): Directly validates her feelings of exhaustion and acknowledges her effort before jumping to solutions.

options.text: I can take over slides 15 through 30 tonight if you send me the Figma link and update Jira ticket #3402.
options.feedback: MISMATCH (Practical Overreach): Jumping straight to task delegation ignores her emotional state. Match first, then solve.

options.text: You should set up a Notion workflow template so revision requests don't take as long in the future.
options.feedback: MISMATCH (Unsolicited Optimization): Giving advice when someone is venting creates resentment. She needs empathy, not a tool recommendation.

core_takeaway: When someone is in an Emotional state (venting/exhaustion), matching requires validating feelings first. Never force positivity or jump straight into optimization.

context: Your coworker Marcus texts you: 'Hey, do you know if the Q3 budget spreadsheet was submitted to Finance yet? I need the row 14 line item totals for the VP meeting in 15 mins.'
prompt: How do you respond to Marcus to MATCH his current conversation state?

options.text: Yes, just sent! Row 14 line item total is $42,500. Here's the direct link: drive.google.com/q3-budget.
options.feedback: CORRECT (Practical Matching): Marcus is strictly in a Practical state with high time urgency. Delivering exact data concisely matches his state.

options.text: Oh man VP meetings are so stressful! Take a deep breath, you're going to crush it no matter what!
options.feedback: MISMATCH (Emotional Overreach): Marcus didn't ask for emotional coaching; he has a 15-minute deadline and needs practical data immediately.

options.text: I was just thinking about how hard our team works together. We really have great chemistry on these quarterly budgets!
options.feedback: MISMATCH (Social Drift): Bringing up team bonding when a colleague needs urgent metrics causes friction.

options.text: Why does Finance always demand these last minute? They should really streamline their intake process.
options.feedback: MISMATCH (Unhelpful Venting): Adding commentary delays answering his urgent question.

core_takeaway: Practical conversations demand quick, precise, actionable answers. Avoid emotional or social detours when time-critical information is requested.

context: During the pre-meeting chatter on a Zoom call, Maya mentions: 'I saw a few of us are based in Chicago—anyone going to the design meetup downtown this Thursday? Trying to get to know more people on the team outside of project syncs!'
prompt: How do you respond to Maya to MATCH her conversation state?

options.text: I'm in Chicago! I'd love to go together or grab a coffee beforehand. Great idea to connect outside of work!
options.feedback: CORRECT (Social Matching): Maya is initiating a Social conversation around identity and community. Reciprocating warmth and connection matches her state.

options.text: Let me share the agenda for today's call so we stay on track for our 30-minute block.
options.feedback: MISMATCH (Practical Shutdown): Shutting down social connection rapport-building harms team cohesion.

options.text: It must be really scary and intimidating moving to a big city like Chicago alone.
options.feedback: MISMATCH (Projected Emotion): Maya expressed enthusiasm for meeting people, not fear or distress.

options.text: Here is an Excel list of all employees organized by zip code for optimal networking efficiency.
options.feedback: MISMATCH (Unsolicited Optimization): Replacing human connection with cold administrative tools misses the social intent.

core_takeaway: Social state conversations focus on identity, belonging, and connection. Respond with warmth and mutual interest before pivoting to agenda items.

context: In a 1-on-1 coffee chat, your direct report Alex leans back and sighs: 'I feel like no matter how much effort I put into these pitch decks, leadership only notices when there's a typo on slide 3. It makes me question if I'm even built for this role.'
prompt: Using Duhigg's 'Looping for Understanding' technique, which response best matches Alex's state?

options.text: What I'm hearing is that you feel unappreciated for your hard work, and the focus on small mistakes makes you doubt your impact here. Is that right?
options.feedback: CORRECT (Looping for Understanding): Distills his emotional core, reflects it back, and asks for confirmation to build deep trust.

options.text: You just need to run Grammarly Premium before every presentation so leadership has nothing to critique.
options.feedback: MISMATCH (Unsolicited Optimization): Solves the superficial typo issue while ignoring his deeper existential self-doubt.

options.text: Leadership is just under a lot of pressure right now, you shouldn't take it personally at all!
options.feedback: MISMATCH (Toxic Positivity / Defense): Defending leadership invalidates Alex's feelings and cuts off open dialogue.

options.text: Let's review your quarterly KPIs to see if your overall rating qualifies for a promotion.
options.feedback: MISMATCH (Practical Overreach): Shifting to cold metrics when someone expresses vulnerability damages rapport.

core_takeaway: Looping for Understanding requires 3 steps: 1) Listen carefully, 2) Summarize what you heard in your own words, 3) Ask 'Did I get that right?' to confirm.

context: In a product design channel, Senior Engineer David writes: 'The API response latency spiked to 450ms after the latest deployment. We need to decide whether to roll back build v2.4 or deploy the hotfix patch within the next hour.'
prompt: How do you respond to David to MATCH his conversation state?

options.text: Let's look at the telemetry metrics: if the hotfix passes staging unit tests in 15 mins, deploy patch; otherwise roll back immediately.
options.feedback: CORRECT (Practical Matching): Directly addresses the decision framework and criteria David requested.

options.text: Deployments are always so nerve-wracking! Everyone stay calm, we'll get through this together! ❤️
options.feedback: MISMATCH (Emotional Overreach): Emotional cheerleading doesn't resolve technical latency spikes.

options.text: Who was the engineer responsible for pushing build v2.4 without stress testing?
options.feedback: MISMATCH (Blame Assignment): Blaming individuals during an active incident creates fear instead of resolving the practical issue.

options.text: We should organize a team dinner after this release to celebrate our hard work!
options.feedback: MISMATCH (Social Drift): Irrelevant social planning during a live technical escalation.

core_takeaway: In high-urgency practical scenarios, focus strictly on decision logic, metrics, and immediate mitigation steps.

context: Your colleague Jordan texts: 'Hey! A few of us from the remote team are forming a fantasy football league this season. Want in? No pressure at all, just for fun!'
prompt: Which response best MATCHES Jordan's conversation state?

options.text: Count me in! Sounds like a blast, thanks for inviting me to join the group! 🏈
options.feedback: CORRECT (Social Matching): Matches the social invitation with enthusiastic inclusion and group connection.

options.text: Can you send me an ROI analysis on time spent managing a fantasy roster vs workplace productivity?
options.feedback: MISMATCH (Over-Analytical Practical): Treating a social invitation like a corporate audit kills social warmth.

options.text: I'm feeling really stressed about my workload so I don't have emotional bandwidth for sports.
options.feedback: MISMATCH (Unnecessary Heavy Emotion): Declining is fine, but heavy emotional dumping onto a casual social invite creates awkwardness.

options.text: Fantasy sports are statistically biased toward draft order position.
options.feedback: MISMATCH (Pedantic Buzzkill): Being pedantic shuts down casual camaraderie.

core_takeaway: Social state invitations build team social capital. Respond in kind with lighthearted connection or polite social gratitude.
